residuals.detail: Rugra's public production entry returns () and adapts the Result-bearing core to panic; locked Ghidra throws LowlevelError. Identical payload text is not identical exception-channel behavior.

AddressSpace::Other(non-1) has lost AddrSpace::getType. The implementation fails closed, so a custom IPTR_PROCESSOR or IPTR_SPACEBASE space represented by Other(non-1) is skipped. Locked translate.cc:47-60 permits multiple SpacebaseSpace instances with arbitrary indices, so the SPACEBASE half is not limited to the fixed stack projection.

mergeAddrTied now creates real pieces. A later required merge with two grouped HighVariables still hits the pre-existing debug_assert/release-false arm instead of variable.cc:699-711 mergeGroups behavior. With exactly one side grouped, merge_highs reaches variable.rs merge_internal, whose existing numMergeClasses branch logs and continues instead of throwing after the locked dirty-flag/symbol and piece-transfer mutations at variable.cc:631-650. Both grouped closure and one-group merge-class error semantics are source-proven mismatches.

Forced cover intersection, pre-existing group ownership cases, duplicate-piece partial mutation, and the neither-grouped speculative merge-class branch lack bilateral production fixtures. The Result core contains explicit handling but no MATCH claim is made; grouped speculative merge classes are separately recorded as a source-proven mismatch.

The transitive fixture observes an input followed by written instances, but creates them in that same order and assigns written SeqNums in creation order. It therefore does not distinguish VarnodeCompareLocDef input precedence or written SeqNum ordering from creation-index ordering.

The C++ observer canonicalizes group identity and reconstructs/sorts tracked pieces by (offset,size), so the bilateral 0/4/10 output proves offsets, size, membership, and that projected order but not native VariableGroup pieceSet comparator/iteration order. The error case begins with only I0/I1 and encounters IMPLIED before any successful exact-run merge, so mergeRangeMust partial-mutation/traversal timing after an earlier merge is untested. Its projection covers the emitted payload plus observed Varnode/High/group/topology fields, but does not close High cover/type/nameRep/symbolOffset, Varnode mergegroup/cover/type/addlflags, piece intersection/cover, group symbolOffset, Merge caches/copyTrims, or exact op-edge mutation.

The transitive case proves overlap extension and exclusion when the next run begins one byte after the inclusive max, but has no run beginning exactly at the current max, so <= versus < remains unseparated. Space gating is bilateral only for register, ram, locked OTHER@index1, stack, unique, and join; Overlay, Iop/Fspec, and Const variants are not claimed.
The surrounding Action chain still constructs local Merge values and cannot propagate Result/LowlevelError through the production caller boundary under this slice's write lease.

Locked mergeAddrTied has no alive/live_set gate, but opUninsert leaves a written output whose defining op has null parent; unifyAddress immediately feeds it to BlockVarnode::set, which dereferences getParent. The legal merge-stage fixture therefore does not synthesize this unparented intermediate state. The Rust projection deliberately does not add a merge-layer live_set filter.
